summary.intent: Win the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge by analyzing Soony's launch data, then building a general agent product that rechecks plans against documents, flags contradictions and takes real supplier actions (emails, calls, routines).
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses launch and spotted the Standard game-card shortfall, then built a polling and versioned-store backend, a paper-check verifier, routines with trust levels and a calm 'Today' UI. Work is pushed to branch jonas/today-flow; automation-in-Today, restyle and single-view routine builders were still running.

repo: Portal API has only three endpoints (files list, single file, archive.zip) and no webhooks. Files get replaced under the same name, so change detection must compare SHA-256 per file and handle format drift.
Data lives in gitignored data/ (raw, drops, notes, state, design); .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and .env.example is committed. Confidential portal data must never be committed or put in code.
Team workflow files CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md require claiming tasks in PROGRESS.md and Entire/Brain checks before pushing. Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change.

Verifier counts inbound only when the supplier document confirms it. Without a recognizer reading of the Hwaseong shipping advice the game-card gap shows 34,800; with it, 6,800 matching the paper check.
The image recognizer put part numbers in the `item` field with an empty `material_id`, so the linker needed a part-number fallback to recognize the short shipment.
New routines now default to 'ask' mode, and saving a new routine version keeps its mode. Legacy code-only routines have no recipe and cannot render a diagram.
Voice decisions now use a two-step prepare-then-decide flow with a one-time token, so the assistant cannot decide without announcing the action first.

code.finding: Each part now carries `arriving` and `not_counted` lists, and gap = needed - usable - arriving. Arrivals are counted only if ETA is on or before launch, not cancelled, not already received, not overdue, and the supplier document doesn't say less.
The wide view was restructured into When/Then/Always lanes that wrap, with the dashed 'You decide' brake under send steps. The narrow vertical view is unchanged.
The watcher loop was replaced by the team runner loop so the team pipeline runs in the server process.

workflow: Subagents were split by file ownership (front-end builder, verifier fixer, restyle builder) so parallel edits didn't conflict.
Paid API calls, pushes and real supplier emails were gated on explicit user approval. Live checks on real data were view-only, and screenshot checks used mocked POSTs.
Test suites were run before each commit, and tests that pinned old behavior were updated when defaults changed.

friction: Entire initially seemed not to fire because no checkpoint is written when no repo files changed; Codex hooks still need approval.
The dashboard showed 34,800 vs the correct 6,800 until a paid recognizer reading was approved and a linker mapping bug was fixed.
The UI offered Undo after an email was sent, and the voice assistant said it would outline the action but just reported 'done', both misleading.
Legacy code-only routines didn't render diagrams and one failed against the changed building blocks.
The routine view had redundant Flow/Steps/Expanded modes, and the first wide diagram was a single long line.
The Teams header emoji replacement missed a multi-line match and had to be fixed manually.
The sleeping teammate Farhan owned the verifier, so the fix was made without his input and only left a note.
open_items: Open a PR from jonas/today-flow into main and close the stale PR #5, or let Akshat merge.
Finish and verify the in-flight builders: automation inside Today ('Show me how' wide diagram, proposals review), routine single-view editor and restyle of Plan/Suppliers/evidence/login.
Hand-in by 12:00 Sunday: README section, demo script, 3-minute video, deck.
Verifier leftovers: the 'runs dry' time ignores arrivals, and impact/__main__.py doesn't print the arriving list.
Standard's 32,000 game-card-case risk comes from the port collect card; the user may want it shown as 'fixable by collecting' in amber.
Register sender addresses in portal Settings, and send the Karton Nowak art-book order (offer valid 24 h) and the Boise terms reply through the product.
Delete data/state.json snapshot and the briefing pages after the hack, as they hold portal data; a chat-shared portal password should be changed.
Phone Approve without a price sends a real supplier email immediately; decide whether to keep that.
The Plan view is still dense, and the earlier briefing doc and page may need cleanup.
